question: A generator instance is instructed: 'Before you finish, re-read your changes and point out any mistakes.' The team observes this rarely surfaces issues that a fresh reviewer later finds. What best explains this?
options: A) The generator is still in the session where it already committed to its design decisions, so it is less likely to question choices it just justified
B) The instruction is phrased as a command rather than a question, and rephrasing it as a question would make the model more critical of its own output
C) The generator's extended thinking is disabled by default, so it never allocates any reasoning tokens to the re-read step at all
D) The generator lacks access to the files it just wrote, so it cannot literally re-read the changes it is being asked to critique
correct_answers: A) The generator is still in the session where it already committed to its design decisions, so it is less likely to question choices it just justified
explanations: Correct. This is the self-review limitation: retained reasoning context from generation makes the model less likely to question decisions it already made in the same session.
Incorrect. Phrasing the instruction as a question doesn't remove the retained reasoning context that causes the underlying limitation.
Incorrect. Extended thinking availability is unrelated to the root cause; even with extended thinking enabled, the same-session bias remains.
Incorrect. The generator typically still has file access; the limitation is about retained reasoning bias, not missing tool access.
